title_en: Throttle position sensor A: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the throttle position sensor circuit, so it cannot read the throttle opening reliably.
likely_causes_en: Worn or faulty throttle position sensor
Damaged wiring or loose connector at the sensor
Sensor loose or out of position on the throttle body
rider_advice_en: Idle may be uneven and throttle response may feel poor or jerky. Ride gently and get it checked soon; stop and check sooner if the engine stalls or surges.
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor connector for water, corrosion and bent pins
Wiggle the harness while watching the throttle reading on the scan tool
Look for a smooth, jump-free reading from closed to fully open

title_en: Intake manifold pressure (MAP) sensor: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the intake pressure sensor circuit, so it cannot judge engine load or air pressure correctly.
likely_causes_en: Cracked or loose vacuum hose to the sensor
rider_advice_en: The engine may run rough, lose power or be hard to start. Get it checked soon and avoid hard riding until it is fixed.
technician_hints_en: Inspect the vacuum hose to the sensor for cracks, kinks and loose ends
Compare the pressure reading at key-on with the outside air pressure
Check the connector and wiring for water and corrosion

title_en: Engine oil temperature sensor: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the engine oil temperature sensor circuit, so the oil temperature reading is missing or unreliable.
rider_advice_en: The bike should ride normally, but the ECU may not notice a hot engine. Watch for signs of overheating and get the sensor checked at the next service.
technician_hints_en: Check the connector and wiring for oil, heat damage and corrosion
Compare with the engine temperature reading after a cold start

title_en: Oxygen (O2) sensor, upstream: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the upstream oxygen sensor circuit, so it cannot fine-tune the fuel mixture from the exhaust gas reading.
likely_causes_en: Sensor wiring chafed against the exhaust
rider_advice_en: The bike may run richer, use more fuel and fail an emission check. It usually rides normally, but get it checked soon to protect the emission system.
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor harness for melting or chafing near the exhaust
Check the connector for water and corrosion
Watch the sensor reading switch between rich and lean when warm

title_en: Oxygen sensor heater (upstream): circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the heater circuit of the upstream oxygen sensor, so the sensor warms up slowly or not at all.
likely_causes_en: Open heater element in the oxygen sensor
Blown heater fuse or faulty relay
rider_advice_en: Fuel mixture control is delayed after starting, so emissions and fuel use may rise. Get it checked soon; the bike usually rides normally.
technician_hints_en: Check the heater fuse or relay, if fitted
Check the sensor connector for water and corrosion
Confirm the sensor starts working soon after a cold start

title_en: Fuel injector, cylinder 1: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the cylinder 1 injector circuit, so that cylinder may get no fuel or the wrong amount.
likely_causes_en: Fault in the ECU injector driver (less common)
rider_action_basis: engine may stall or cut out
rider_advice_en: The engine may misfire, lose power or stop. Pull over safely, switch off and check before riding further; get it repaired before continuing.
technician_hints_en: Check the injector connector for water, corrosion and bent pins
Listen for the injector clicking while cranking
Check the injector wiring for chafing

title_en: Ignition coil A, cylinder 1: primary or secondary circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the ignition coil A circuit for cylinder 1, so the spark may be weak or missing.
likely_causes_en: Failed ignition coil (open or shorted winding)
Fault in the ECU ignition driver (less common)
rider_advice_en: The engine may misfire, run on one cylinder or stop. Pull over safely and check before riding further; a long misfire can also damage the emission system.
technician_hints_en: Check the coil connector for water and corrosion
On a two-coil bike, swap the coils to see if the fault moves
Check the ignition wiring for chafing

title_en: Fuel pump control: primary circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the primary circuit that switches the fuel pump, so the pump may not run.
rider_action_basis: no fuel: may stall or not start
rider_advice_en: The engine may be hard to start or may stall without warning. Pull over safely and check before riding further instead of repeatedly trying to restart it.
technician_hints_en: Listen for the fuel pump running for a few seconds at key-on
Check the relay (if fitted) and the connectors for corrosion
Check the pump wiring for chafing and loose connectors

title_en: Crankshaft position sensor A: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the crankshaft position sensor circuit, so it may not know engine speed and position for spark and fuel.
rider_action_basis: engine may stall or not start
rider_advice_en: The engine may stall, cut out or refuse to start. Pull over safely and check before riding further.
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor connector and wiring for heat damage and oil
Check the ring teeth for damage or metal debris
Check that engine speed shows on the scan tool while cranking

title_en: Intake air temperature sensor: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the intake air temperature sensor circuit, so it cannot correct the fuelling for air temperature.
rider_advice_en: The bike usually rides normally, though cold starting or fuel use may be slightly off. Get the sensor checked at the next service.
technician_hints_en: Check the connector for water and corrosion
Compare the reading with the outside air temperature on a cold bike

title_en: Engine (coolant) temperature sensor: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the engine temperature sensor circuit, so it cannot tell how hot the engine is.
rider_advice_en: The bike may be hard to start when cold, idle wrongly or overheat if cooling control is affected. Get it checked soon and watch the temperature gauge.
technician_hints_en: Check the connector for coolant seepage, water and corrosion
Compare the reading with the temperature gauge on a cold and a warm engine

title_en: Fuel injector, cylinder 2: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the cylinder 2 injector circuit, so that cylinder may get no fuel or the wrong amount.
rider_action_basis: engine may stall or cut out
rider_advice_en: One cylinder may get no fuel, causing misfire, rough running or sudden power loss. Pull over safely and check before riding further.
technician_hints_en: Check the injector connector for water, corrosion and bent pins
Listen for the injector clicking while cranking

title_en: Ignition coil B, cylinder 2: primary or secondary circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the ignition coil B circuit for cylinder 2, so the spark may be weak or missing.
likely_causes_en: Failed ignition coil (open or shorted winding)
rider_advice_en: The engine may misfire, run on one cylinder or stop. Pull over safely and check before riding further; a long misfire can also damage the emission system.
technician_hints_en: Check the coil connector for water and corrosion
Swap the coils to see if the fault moves to the other cylinder
Check the ignition wiring for chafing

title_en: Random or multiple cylinder misfire detected
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) detected misfires on more than one cylinder or at random, so combustion is incomplete.
likely_causes_en: Low fuel pressure or weak fuel supply
rider_advice_en: Expect rough running, jerking or loss of power. Reduce load and get it checked soon; stop if the warning lamp blinks or the engine runs very rough, as unburnt fuel can damage the emission system.
technician_hints_en: Read the freeze-frame data to see when the misfire happens
Check the spark plugs and ignition coils first
Check for intake air leaks and fuel supply problems

title_en: Cylinder 1 misfire detected
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) detected misfires on cylinder 1, so that cylinder is not burning its fuel properly.
likely_causes_en: Worn or fouled spark plug on cylinder 1
Blocked or leaking injector on cylinder 1
rider_advice_en: Expect rough running, jerking or loss of power. Reduce load and get it checked soon; stop if the warning lamp blinks or the engine runs very rough, as unburnt fuel can damage the emission system.
technician_hints_en: Read the freeze-frame data to see when the misfire happens
Check the spark plug and ignition coil on this cylinder first
Check the injector and compression if spark is good

title_en: Cylinder 2 misfire detected
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) detected misfires on cylinder 2, so that cylinder is not burning its fuel properly.
likely_causes_en: Worn or fouled spark plug on cylinder 2
Blocked or leaking injector on cylinder 2
rider_advice_en: Expect rough running, jerking or loss of power. Reduce load and get it checked soon; stop if the warning lamp blinks or the engine runs very rough, as unburnt fuel can damage the emission system.
technician_hints_en: Read the freeze-frame data to see when the misfire happens
Check the spark plug and ignition coil on this cylinder first
Check the injector if spark is good

title_en: Fuel mixture too lean
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) is adding extra fuel to keep the mixture right, which means the engine is getting too much air or too little fuel.
likely_causes_en: Weak fuel pump or low fuel pressure
rider_advice_en: The engine may hesitate, run rough or lose power, and a lean mixture can run hot. Get it checked soon and avoid hard or long rides until it is fixed.
technician_hints_en: Look for cracked intake parts and loose hoses
Check fuel supply and injector condition
Compare the fuel trim values at idle and at steady cruise

title_en: Fuel mixture too rich
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) is removing fuel to keep the mixture right, which means the engine is getting too much fuel or too little air.
rider_action_basis: rich mixture can harm emission system
rider_advice_en: Expect black smoke, a fuel smell or poor mileage. A rich mixture can damage the emission system, so get it checked soon.
technician_hints_en: Check the air filter and intake for blockage
Check for fuel smell and injector leakage
Check that the oxygen sensor reading is changing

title_en: Catalytic converter efficiency below threshold
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) judges that the catalytic converter is not cleaning the exhaust as well as expected.
likely_causes_en: Exhaust leak before the catalytic converter
rider_advice_en: The bike usually rides normally, but emissions may be above the limit. Get it checked at the next service; fix any misfire or exhaust leak first.
technician_hints_en: Check for exhaust leaks before the catalytic converter
Compare the upstream and downstream oxygen sensor readings
Fix any misfire or fuel mixture code first

title_en: Throttle position sensor A: voltage below threshold
meaning_en: The throttle position sensor signal is lower than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, often from a short to ground or a missing sensor supply.
likely_causes_en: Sensor supply missing at the connector
rider_advice_en: Throttle response may feel poor, idle may be uneven and the ECU may limit power. Ride gently and get it checked soon.
technician_hints_en: Check the connector and wiring for chafing, water and corrosion
Check that the sensor supply and ground reach the connector
Watch the throttle reading on the scan tool while turning the throttle

title_en: Throttle position sensor A: voltage above threshold
meaning_en: The throttle position sensor signal is higher than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, often from a short to battery supply or a broken sensor ground.
likely_causes_en: Signal wire short to battery supply
rider_advice_en: Throttle response may feel poor, idle may be high or uneven and the ECU may limit power. Ride gently and get it checked soon.
technician_hints_en: Check the connector and wiring for chafing, water and corrosion
Check the sensor ground connection
Watch the throttle reading on the scan tool while turning the throttle

title_en: Intake manifold pressure (MAP) sensor: voltage below threshold
meaning_en: The intake pressure sensor signal is lower than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, often from a short to ground or a missing sensor supply.
likely_causes_en: Sensor supply missing at the connector
rider_advice_en: The engine may run rough, lose power or be hard to start. Get it checked soon and avoid hard riding until it is fixed.
technician_hints_en: Check the connector and wiring for chafing, water and corrosion
Compare the pressure reading at key-on with the outside air pressure

title_en: Intake manifold pressure (MAP) sensor: voltage above threshold
meaning_en: The intake pressure sensor signal is higher than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, often from a short to battery supply or a broken sensor ground.
likely_causes_en: Signal wire short to battery supply
rider_advice_en: The engine may run rich, lose power or be hard to start. Get it checked soon and avoid hard riding until it is fixed.
technician_hints_en: Check the connector and wiring for chafing, water and corrosion
Compare the pressure reading at key-on with the outside air pressure

title_en: Intake air temperature sensor: voltage below threshold
meaning_en: The intake air temperature signal is lower than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, so the air looks hotter than it is; often a short to ground.
rider_advice_en: The bike usually rides normally, though fuel use or cold starting may be slightly off. Get the sensor checked at the next service.
technician_hints_en: Check the wiring for chafing and the connector for water
Compare the reading with the outside air temperature on a cold bike

title_en: Intake air temperature sensor: voltage above threshold
meaning_en: The intake air temperature signal is higher than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, so the air looks colder than it is; often an open circuit.
likely_causes_en: Open circuit in the sensor or wiring
rider_advice_en: The bike usually rides normally, though fuel use or cold starting may be slightly off. Get the sensor checked at the next service.
technician_hints_en: Check the connector for corrosion and a loose fit
Compare the reading with the outside air temperature on a cold bike

title_en: Engine (coolant) temperature sensor: voltage below threshold
meaning_en: The engine temperature signal is lower than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, so the engine looks hotter than it is; often a short to ground.
rider_advice_en: The bike may be hard to start when cold and stumble until warm. Get it checked soon and watch the temperature gauge for signs of overheating.
technician_hints_en: Check the wiring for chafing and the connector for water
Compare the reading with the temperature gauge on a cold engine

title_en: Engine (coolant) temperature sensor: voltage above threshold
meaning_en: The engine temperature signal is higher than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, so the engine looks colder than it is; often an open circuit.
likely_causes_en: Open circuit in the sensor or wiring
rider_advice_en: The bike may run rich, smoke or use more fuel, and cooling may not switch on when needed. Get it checked soon and watch the temperature gauge for overheating.
technician_hints_en: Check the connector for corrosion and a loose fit
Compare the reading with the temperature gauge on a warm engine

title_en: Oxygen (O2) sensor, upstream: voltage below threshold
meaning_en: The upstream oxygen sensor signal stays lower than expected, from a lean mixture, an exhaust leak or a short to ground.
likely_causes_en: Lean running (air leak or low fuel supply)
rider_advice_en: The engine may hesitate or run rough, and emissions may rise. Get it checked soon; the bike usually rides normally.
technician_hints_en: Check the exhaust joints before the sensor for leaks
Check the sensor wiring for chafing near the exhaust
Check for intake air leaks and low fuel supply

title_en: Oxygen (O2) sensor, upstream: voltage above threshold
meaning_en: The upstream oxygen sensor signal stays higher than expected, from a rich mixture, a contaminated sensor or a short to battery supply.
likely_causes_en: Rich running (leaking injector or high fuel pressure)
Signal wire short to battery supply
Sensor contaminated by silicone or coolant
rider_advice_en: Expect poor mileage, black smoke or a fuel smell, and a rich mixture can damage the emission system. Get it checked soon.
technician_hints_en: Check the injectors and fuel pressure for a rich condition
Check the sensor wiring for chafing and heat damage
Look for silicone sealant or coolant contamination

title_en: Vehicle speed sensor A: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) is not getting a reliable vehicle speed signal from the speed sensor circuit.
rider_advice_en: The speedometer may read wrongly or not at all, and idle control may be affected. Get it checked soon and do not rely on the speedometer meanwhile.
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor connector and wiring for damage and water
Compare the speed shown on the scan tool with the speedometer

title_en: System voltage below threshold (battery or charging)
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) sees the electrical system voltage lower than expected, which points to a weak battery or poor charging.
likely_causes_en: Corroded battery terminals or loose ground
rider_advice_en: Lights may dim and the bike may be hard to start or stall when the battery runs down. Switch off extra accessories, avoid long rides and get the battery and charging checked soon.
technician_hints_en: Check the battery terminals and ground connections for corrosion and looseness
Check battery condition and charging at idle and at higher engine speed

title_en: System voltage above threshold (overcharging)
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) sees the electrical system voltage higher than expected, which points to a charging system that is overcharging.
rider_advice_en: Overcharging can damage the battery, bulbs and electronics. Get it checked soon; stop and check if lights look unusually bright, bulbs keep failing or the battery gets hot or smells.
technician_hints_en: Check the charging level at idle and at higher engine speed
Check the regulator connector for heat damage and corrosion

title_en: Neutral switch input: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the neutral (gear position) switch input, so it may not know whether the bike is in neutral or in gear.
likely_causes_en: Switch loose or out of position
rider_action_basis: start or idle behaviour may be wrong
rider_advice_en: The bike may not start, or the neutral lamp may show the wrong state. Get it checked soon and do not bypass any safety switch.
technician_hints_en: Check that the neutral lamp lights when the gear is in neutral
Check the switch connector for oil, water and corrosion
Check the switch wiring for chafing

title_en: Serial communication link: fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) reports a fault on its serial communication link, so some control units may not exchange data properly.
likely_causes_en: Damaged wiring on the communication lines
rider_advice_en: Warning lamps, gauges or other functions may behave oddly, and the engine may run poorly. Get it checked soon; stop if the engine cuts out.
technician_hints_en: Check the connectors and wiring on the communication lines for water and chafing
Read all control units for related communication codes
Check the ground and supply connections of the control units

title_en: Camshaft position sensor A: circuit fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the camshaft position sensor circuit, so it may lose track of the engine cycle for fuel and spark timing.
likely_causes_en: Worn timing chain affecting the sensor signal
rider_action_basis: may start hard or run rough
rider_advice_en: The engine may be hard to start, run rough or lose power. Get it checked soon; stop and check if the engine stalls repeatedly.
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor connector and wiring for oil, heat damage and corrosion
Check the sensor mounting and its signal while cranking

title_en: Idle control system: fault
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) cannot hold the engine idle speed where it wants it.
likely_causes_en: Sticky or dirty idle air control valve
Air leak after the throttle (vacuum leak)
rider_advice_en: Idle may hunt, run too high or too low, or the engine may stall at stops. Get it checked soon and be ready for a stall in traffic.
technician_hints_en: Clean the throttle body and idle air passage as the service manual says
Check for intake air leaks
Compare commanded and actual idle speed on the scan tool

title_en: Engine computer (ECU): communication lost
meaning_en: Another unit or the scan tool could not get messages from the bike's computer (ECU), so the ECU may be unpowered or cut off from the network.
likely_causes_en: ECU not powered (fuse, ground or supply wire)
Broken communication wiring to the ECU
rider_advice_en: The engine may run poorly, cut out or not start, and warning lamps may light up. Get it checked soon; stop and check if the engine cuts out.
technician_hints_en: Check the ECU fuse, ground and supply connections
Check the communication wiring and connectors for damage
Check whether other control units also show communication lost codes

title_en: ABS control unit: communication lost
meaning_en: Another control unit could not get messages from the ABS control unit, so ABS may be switched off.
likely_causes_en: ABS unit not powered (blown fuse or corroded ground)
Broken communication wiring to the ABS unit
rider_advice_en: Normal braking should still work, but ABS may be off and a wheel can lock under hard braking. Ride gently, brake early and get it checked soon.
technician_hints_en: Check the ABS fuse, ground and supply connections
Check the communication wiring and connectors for damage
Check whether the ABS warning lamp behaves normally at key-on

title_en: Instrument cluster: communication lost
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) or another unit could not get messages from the instrument cluster.
likely_causes_en: Cluster not powered (blown fuse or poor ground)
Broken communication wiring to the cluster
rider_action_basis: gauges and lamps may not work
rider_advice_en: The speedometer, fuel gauge or warning lamps may not work, so you may miss a warning. Get it checked soon and ride carefully.
technician_hints_en: Check the cluster fuse, ground and supply connections
Check the communication wiring and connectors for damage

title_en: Wheel speed sensor (listed as left front): circuit fault
meaning_en: The ABS control unit found a fault in a wheel speed sensor circuit, so ABS may be switched off.
rider_advice_en: Normal braking should still work, but ABS may be off and a wheel can lock under hard braking. Ride gently, brake early, avoid wet roads and get it checked soon.
technician_hints_en: A bike has front and rear sensors only; check the maker's table for the wheel
Check the sensor gap and the tone ring for dirt and damage
Check the sensor wiring for chafing and the connector for water
